question: A brand team is running a brainstorming session for a new ad campaign and wants Claude to keep generating fresh concepts rather than settling on the first workable idea. Which instruction best supports this goal?
options: A) Ask Claude to keep generating distinct concepts after producing a workable one
B) Ask Claude to rate its own first concept highly to bias later comparisons
C) Ask Claude to stop once it produces a concept fitting the campaign brief nicely
D) Ask Claude to expand only on the first concept in greater detail
correct_answers: A) Ask Claude to keep generating distinct concepts after producing a workable one
explanations: Correct. Explicitly asking for continued generation of distinct concepts keeps a brainstorming session open rather than converging on the first workable answer.
Incorrect. Pre-rating the first concept highly biases the comparison against later ideas rather than encouraging open generation of fresh concepts.
Incorrect. Stopping at the first workable concept defeats the purpose of a brainstorming session meant to surface a range of fresh ideas.
Incorrect. Elaborating only on the first concept narrows the session into refining one idea instead of generating a variety of new ones.
